artifacts.summary: Reclassified bare/whole-tree git stash as destructive on a shared working tree: corrected the rule's wrong premise, added a stash_revert guard detector wired into both existing escape hatches, landed a red-then-green fixture, and redeployed with a fully green gate set.

completion_data.completion_summary: Corrected rules/git-workflow.md's wrong premise (bare git stash was listed 'Not blocked' though it reverts the tree under concurrent writers), implemented a new stash_revert detector in guard-destructive-git.sh covering bare/push/implicit-push/-u forms while exempting pathspec-scoped stash and recovery forms, wired the class into both the snapshot-marker and /please grant escape hatches, demonstrated the fixture red-then-green, and redeployed with verify-deploy.sh's full gate set green (the sole remaining finding is 4 pre-existing, unrelated run-all.sh suite failures, 0 new).

memory_candidates.content: This repo's orchestrator eager-context budget gate (Gate 20 in verify-deploy.sh, orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.baseline_bytes) is a FIXED ceiling that must never be silently re-derived -- its own file history shows every prior overage resolved by COMPRESSING the eager-loaded rule text (moving extended reasoning into the companion non-eager context/standards/*-narrative.md file the rule already points to), never by moving the baseline. Editing any file matched by a broad eager-load path glob (e.g. rules/git-workflow.md, which is eager per its own path pattern) -- even a seemingly small addition -- can push the measured total over baseline; re-measure with 'REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check' after any such edit, not just at redeploy time. Pattern: write the full reasoning in the narrative file FIRST, then write only a minimal pointer-plus-verdict in the eager rule, rather than writing verbose rule prose and trimming later.

In push-grant-lib.sh's destructive-action-class machinery, pg_grant_mint does NOT validate PG_ACTION_CLASSES membership for any class name -- it will happily mint a grant for a bogus/unregistered class. It is pg_grant_consume/pg_grant_verify (the function guard-destructive-git.sh's grant check actually calls) that fails closed on an unregistered name. This matters when verifying a new class's wiring end-to-end: testing only 'does pg_grant_mint succeed' proves nothing about fail-closed behavior; test pg_grant_consume (or the full guard-hook round trip) instead.

During a multi-phase implementation task that is mid-flight (source store ahead of the deployed .claude/ tree, not yet redeployed), a full verify-deploy.sh / run-all.sh run will surface gate3/gate5 content-drift findings for every file the task has edited so far -- this is EXPECTED and resolves automatically once the task's final redeploy phase runs; it is not a regression. One specific downstream symptom: scripts/tests/test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh's fixture rsync-copies the live agent-system/extensions/ tree (picking up the task's in-flight edits) while symlinking .claude/ to the real, not-yet-redeployed tree, so its own 'baseline fixture is clean' assumption breaks and run-all.sh classifies it as a 'NEW' failure (not in known-failures.txt) purely because of this timing artifact. Confirm by re-running after the task's redeploy: if it now passes, the 'NEW' classification was this artifact, not a real defect.
